messages:
anya: quick pulse: bringing up 'manta-embed-lite' on dedicated staging. ran recall@1/5/10 across paraphrase holdout. float16 baseline recall@1=0.79, int8=0.78, int6-perchannel=0.75. interestingly, multilingual cohort (es/pt) had higher degradation.
ravi: multilingual often suffers because tokenization leads to different embedding distributions. what tokenizer did you use?
anya: sentencepiece v0.1.96, vocab commit b9f7c. same tokenizer used for baseline. eval holdout contains ~3k queries English + 1k Spanish + 700 Portugese.
sam: any chance that byte-pair boundaries changed? even small merges can shift embedding geometry.
anya: confirmed tokenizer identical. suspect quant scales biased by majority English calibration. redoing calibration with stratified sample proportional to lang distribution. also trying per-channel calibration per-language.
ops-bot: staging deploy: manta-lite-int6-perch (per-channel) rolled at 2025-04-20T11:04Z.
anya: per-lang calib preliminary: recall@1 for es improved from 0.66 -> 0.72; pt 0.63 -> 0.69; overall int6 now 0.76. idflip reduced from 6.1% -> 3.4% after per-lang calib.
ravi: good. can we get cluster purity for lang clusters (k-NN purity)? helps quantify cross-lang bleed.
anya: will compute purity and neighbor overlap. also adding a tiny prompt-agnostic perturbation test (strip accents, remove diacritics) to see robustness.
eng-platform: FYI we can add a routing rule based on language detection to prefer int8 for underperforming langs until quant params stabilize. might be heavier operationally though.
sam: agree but maybe short term solution. we should pursue per-lang calibration as the primary fix.
anya: plan: finish purity metrics, push calibration commits + eval script in PR, request eng-ml review. tag @ravi for tokenizer checks.
anya: attaching quick plot: https://rwd-infra/plots/manta/perlang_recall.png
ops-bot: note: auto rollback disabled for this canary.
